html:
A Turkish-ruled, Persian-speaking empire founded in 1037 by the brothers Tughril and Chaghri of the Oghuz Turks. At its height it ran from Anatolia and the Levant to the Hindu Kush. Its rule outside Anatolia ended in 1194.

The Seljuks were nomads from the steppe north of the Aral Sea who had become Muslim. They beat the Ghaznavids at Dandanaqan in 1040 and took Iran. In 1055 Tughril entered Baghdad as protector of the Abbasid caliph, who gave him the title of sultan. From then on the caliph reigned and the sultan ruled.

High points:

  • Alp Arslan beat the Byzantine emperor at Manzikert in 1071, and Turks began to settle Anatolia.
  • The vizier Nizam al-Mulk ran the state for three decades and founded madrasas, colleges for Sunni law, across the empire.
  • Al-Ghazali taught at the Baghdad college, and Omar Khayyam worked on a new solar calendar for Sultan Malik-Shah.

After Malik-Shah died in 1092 the empire split among relatives. That weakness helped the First Crusade succeed. Sultan Sanjar held the east together for a while, and the Khwarazmians ended the line in Iran in 1194.

A branch, the Sultanate of Rum, ruled much of Anatolia from Konya into the 1300s. Out of its break-up came the Turkish principalities, one of them led by Osman, founder of the Ottoman Empire.
sum: A Turkish-ruled, Persian-speaking empire founded in 1037 by the brothers Tughril and Chaghri of the Oghuz Turks. At its height it ran from Anatolia and the Levant to the Hindu Kush. Its rule outside Anatolia ended in 1194.
